item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00494","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C22","C19","C02"],"selected_candidate_label":"C22","confidence":0.9,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C22 plausibly supplied a material template for the child's central delegation. It assigns the Chairman of the United States Civil Service Commission presidential authority over designated positions, uses the same distinctive delegation formula, and gives him authority to place positions in and remove positions from a defined category. The child adapts that machinery to designations under the Annual and Sick Leave Act and to adding positions to or deleting them from an attached schedule. C19 is closely related by statute and delegation formula, but delegates a different leave authority to department and agency heads and lacks the child's position-list maintenance mechanism. C02 shares the delegation formula but is less closely aligned administratively.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"The Chairman of the United States Civil Service Commission is hereby designated and empowered, without the approval, ratification, or other action of the President, to exercise the authority conferred upon the President","parent_excerpt":"The Chairman of the United States Civil Service Commission is hereby designated and empowered, without the approval, ratification, or other action of the President, to exercise the authority vested in the President","explanation":"Near-verbatim, officer-specific delegation language appears in C22 shortly before the child."},{"child_excerpt":"The authority delegated by this paragraph to the Chairman of the Civil Service Commission shall be deemed to include the authority to add positions to, or delete positions from, the schedule of positions attached hereto","parent_excerpt":"to place positions in, and to remove positions from, Grade 18 of the General Schedule","explanation":"Both confer on the same official continuing authority to add and remove positions from a defined administrative category, a concrete machinery adapted in the child to an attached exemption schedule."}]}
